headline: Staff Design Engineer
bio: I live in the seam between design and engineering. Most of my week is spent making sure the thing we shipped actually matches the thing we drew.
working_on: Rebuilding our component library so that spacing and type scale are enforced by tokens instead of by code review. It is deeply unglamorous work and I love it.
curious_about: How other teams handle the handoff between design and engineering without turning it into a bureaucracy. Also variable fonts.
fun_fact: I set my own type specimen posters and print them on a letterpress in my garage.

headline: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
bio: I keep the boring parts running so nobody has to think about them. If you have never heard my name during an incident, I am doing my job.
working_on: Cutting our p99 cold start times by moving the request path off a shared connection pool. Currently arguing with Postgres about lock contention.
curious_about: How teams decide when a service is worth splitting out versus keeping in the monolith. I have strong opinions I would like challenged.
fun_fact: I have run the same 10k loop every Saturday for six years, in four different cities.

headline: Group Product Manager
bio: Recovering consultant. I am happiest turning a vague executive sentence into a roadmap somebody can actually argue with.
working_on: Figuring out what our activation metric should actually be. The current one goes up when we do nothing, which is a bad sign for a metric.
curious_about: How engineers want to be involved in discovery. I suspect we are inviting people to the wrong meetings.
fun_fact: I run a small board game night that has been going for nine years and has its own spreadsheet.

headline: Machine Learning Engineer
bio: I train models and then spend twice as long explaining what they cannot do. Mostly retrieval and ranking these days.
working_on: An embedding-based recommender that has to explain itself. Turning cosine similarity into a sentence a human trusts is harder than the model.
curious_about: Evaluation. Everyone benchmarks, almost nobody agrees on what a good result means for a real product.
fun_fact: I climb, badly but enthusiastically, and I have the finger tape budget to prove it.

headline: Backend Engineer
bio: Ten years of writing services that move money around. I care a lot about correctness and very little about frameworks.
working_on: Migrating our ledger to double-entry properly, which means unpicking four years of well-intentioned shortcuts.
curious_about: How other people test systems where being wrong is expensive. Property-based testing, formal methods, anything.
fun_fact: I bake sourdough on a schedule stricter than our deploy process.

headline: Product Designer
bio: I design the unglamorous middle of products: settings, empty states, error messages. The parts people only notice when they are wrong.
working_on: A full pass on our onboarding. We were asking for eleven things before showing any value, which is ten too many.
curious_about: Writing. I think most design problems turn out to be copy problems wearing a costume.
fun_fact: I keep a photo journal of every hotel carpet I have ever walked on. There are 340.

headline: Engineering Manager
bio: I used to write code and now I write documents about people who write code. It turns out to be the same job with a longer feedback loop.
working_on: Rebuilding how we do career levelling. The current ladder rewards visibility over impact and everyone knows it.
curious_about: How individual contributors actually want to be managed, as opposed to how management books say they do.
fun_fact: I have hiked every waymarked trail in Ireland except one, and I am saving it.

headline: Security Engineer
bio: I think about the ways things break on purpose. Threat modelling, auth flows, and the long tail of mistakes we all keep making.
working_on: A full audit of our row-level security policies. Half of them are correct by accident, which is not the same as correct.
curious_about: How to make security review feel less like a gate and more like a design partner. I have not cracked it.
fun_fact: I compete in lockpicking as a hobby and I am mediocre at it in a very specific way.

headline: Data Scientist
bio: I answer questions with numbers and then explain why the numbers are less certain than they look.
working_on: An experiment framework that stops people from peeking at results early. The statistics are easy, the incentives are the hard part.
curious_about: Causal inference in products where you cannot run a clean experiment. Which is most of them.
fun_fact: I keep bees. They are far more organised than any team I have worked on.

headline: Developer Advocate
bio: I explain our product to engineers and explain engineers to our product team. Both halves involve a lot of demos.
working_on: Rewriting our getting-started guide so it works on a slow connection and a five-year-old laptop, because that is who is actually reading it.
curious_about: What makes technical writing land. I want to talk to anyone who has strong feelings about documentation.
fun_fact: I DJ afrobeats sets at community meetups and I have a genuinely unreasonable vinyl collection.

headline: Frontend Engineer
bio: I build interfaces and then delete half of what I built. Performance and accessibility are the two things I will not compromise on.
working_on: Getting our largest contentful paint under a second on a mid-range Android. Currently at 2.4s and every improvement is a fight.
curious_about: Design systems from the engineering side. How do you keep a token layer honest as it grows?
fun_fact: I cycle-commute 22km each way and know every pothole personally.

headline: Product Manager, Platform
bio: Platform PM, which mostly means my customers are colleagues and my roadmap is other people's unblocking.
working_on: Working out how to measure internal platform adoption without turning it into a vanity metric nobody trusts.
curious_about: Infrastructure. I want to understand the tradeoffs my engineers describe rather than nodding along.
fun_fact: I make furniture on weekends. Three chairs so far, two of which you can sit on.
